_comment: Declared inventory of what this repository publishes THROUGH THE THREE GOVERNED SURFACES listed in coverage.governs, and of the derived files that must agree with it. It is NOT an inventory of every published byte: 179 files under public/ are tracked and deployed and this file names 30 of them; the remaining 149 are covered by a checked disjointness rule (T9), not by enumeration. WHAT THIS GUARANTEES TODAY: nothing is generated FROM this file at runtime yet. deploy/feed-excludes.txt, .gitignore and scripts/push-to-web-host.sh are still hand-maintained and are still what the deploy and the push actually obey. All this file buys, as of C1 Phase 0, is that scripts/deploy/render-publication.sh can reproduce those three regions byte-for-byte from here, and tests/publication-registry/ fails if it ever cannot. That is a detector, not an enforcement: a hand edit to one of those three files that is NOT mirrored here turns the test red, but nothing stops the edit from being made or deployed. Turning consumers around to read this file is C1 Phase 1 and later.

kind_definitions._comment: The taxonomy is defined by ONE measurable question: can these bytes change without a commit to this repository? That question is what decides whether a sha256 pin in a signed manifest can survive, which is the only thing the kind gate acts on.
kind_definitions.stream: Content can change without any commit — host cron, runtime push, or an operator writing straight to the public tree. A pin taken at signing time goes stale on its own. MUST NOT appear in pinned_by.
kind_definitions.record: The URL's NAME is derived from a digest of the content it addresses, so whatever that digest covers cannot change without the name changing too. Safe to pin. CORRECTED 2026-08-14 — this read 'Immutable once written, at a URL that never resolves to different bytes', which is stronger than any record this repository actually publishes. A name binds only what its digest covers, and that need NOT be the whole file: for api/archive/ it is the three DAG branches and not the provenance fields sitting beside them, and the generator overwrites an existing archive unconditionally. What binds every byte is the sha256 in the signed manifest, as of signing. Read the row's record_caveat for how far a given name reaches before pinning on the strength of this kind alone.
kind_definitions.static: Changes only when a commit in this repository changes it, and is delivered by the git deploy. Safe to pin, on the condition that the commit which changes it also re-issues the pin — that condition is what scripts/check-identity-pins.sh enforces.
kind_definitions._kind_is_the_floor: kind is the SAFE FLOOR, never a summary. A consumer that reads only .kind and nothing else must always end up doing the safe thing, so a path is classified by its WEAKEST moment, not its typical one. Qualifier fields (becomes_record_after, record_caveat) may only WIDEN what a consumer that understands them may do; they never narrow what .kind already permits, and a consumer that ignores them stays correct. This is why api/peers-history/ is kind=stream even though every snapshot older than the current UTC day is immutable: at any instant one member is being rewritten, and a consumer pinning on the strength of .kind alone would pin exactly that one.

does_not_govern.surface: The rest of the tracked public/ tree (HTML pages, CSS, JS, images, fonts) — everything under public/ that is neither public/api/* nor public/.well-known/*.
does_not_govern.measured: 149 files: git ls-files public/ = 179 total, git ls-files public/api/ public/.well-known/ = 30, and all 30 of those ARE enumerated in publications[] (T16 fails if that stops being true in either direction). 179 - 30 = 149 unenumerated, 2026-08-07.
does_not_govern.why_excluded: They have exactly one owner (the git deploy), are never pushed, and are never pinned, so there is no lock-step obligation for a registry to hold. tests/publication-registry/ checks the claim rather than assuming it: T9 asserts every tracked file under public/ is disjoint from every feed exclude and every push name, so any of the 149 that ever acquires a second owner is named by a failing test. T16 separately asserts that the two prefixes this file DOES claim (public/api/, public/.well-known/) are enumerated exhaustively — adding a tracked file under either without a row here is a failure.

does_not_govern.surface: /etc/cron.d on the validator host — the cron files that actually invoke the producers.
does_not_govern.measured: Six cron basenames have a creating installer in this repo (metal-host-advance, metal-anchor-watch, metal-anchor-publish-health, metal-identity-pins, metal-host-drift, metal-watch-validators — grep of scripts/install-*.sh for cron.d/, 2026-08-07). NONE of them produces a publication listed here. Of the 20 push-owned publications (publisher push / push-subdir / push-out-of-band), 17 name a cron and ALL 17 carry owner.cron_installer_in_repo=false, i.e. zero of them have a repo-verifiable command body. The other 3 — api/anchor-receipt.json, api/anchor-history.jsonl, api/archive/ — are on NO cron at all and carry cron_installer_in_repo=null; they are produced by hand through scripts/run-anchor-pipeline.sh after an on-chain broadcast. Do not read this as 'push implies cron'.
does_not_govern.why_excluded: A registry cannot govern text it cannot read. The spec (§9) records that 15 project cron files run in production and 7 have no repo installer; that count was measured on the host, not by this file, and is not re-measured here. What IS measured here is the repo side: the schedule, the arguments, and the environment that decide when and where a producer writes are outside this file for every push-owned publication. Do not read owner.producer as 'the registry controls this artifact' — it means only 'this script contains the write'.

does_not_govern.surface: The web host's forced-command receive wrapper (/home/<deploy user>/bin/receive-metal-push).
does_not_govern.measured: Its flat-filename allowlist is operator-local and not in this repo. Only the subdirectory block is (scripts/deploy/receive-subdir-allowlist.snippet.sh), and tests/publication-registry/ checks that block's basename patterns against this file and against the sender.
does_not_govern.why_excluded: Adding a name here and to the sender still leaves the receiver to be changed by hand on the host. A push whose name is new here will be rejected remotely until that happens.

does_not_govern.surface: Whether anything listed here is actually reachable at its public URL right now.
does_not_govern.measured: Not measured. No HTTP request is made by this file or by its tests.
does_not_govern.why_excluded: Phase 0 is offline and hermetic by construction. Liveness is the reconciler's job (spec §9), not the registry's.

publications.record_caveat: CORRECTED 2026-08-14 — neither half of this prefix is immutable by construction, and the superseded text claimed the anchor-source half was. anchor-source-<dag_root>.json: the <dag_root> in the name is dag_root_computed, and scripts/gen-anchor-source.sh:638-641 folds it from the three branch objects and nothing else (identity_branch, observations_branch, artifacts_branch each jq -cS then sha256; dag_root = sha256 of the three hex digests concatenated in that order). The same file also carries computed_at, computed_by_script and computed_from_git_commit as top-level siblings of those branches (scripts/gen-anchor-source.sh:656-658), and none of the three enters the fold; the archive copy is then written with an unconditional rename (:780 builds ARCHIVE_FILE as anchor-source-<DAG_ROOT>.json, :787 renames the temp file onto it), which overwrites whatever already sits at that name. Measured 2026-08-14 against the tracked public/api/anchor-source.json: editing only the computed_at value leaves the root re-derived from the three branches — and therefore the file name — unchanged, while the file's sha256 changes. Reproduce by hashing each of the three branch objects with jq -cS piped to sha256, concatenating the three hex digests in identity/observations/artifacts order and hashing that string. So the URL's name binds the three branch roots; a sha256 in a signed manifest binds the whole file as of signing. identity.json's pin_policy (scripts/operator-local/gen-identity.sh) carries that same wording verbatim, machine-checked against kind_definitions.record by tests/publication-registry/ (T20) and against public/api/identity.example.json by tests/identity-kind-discipline/. CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (the reference in the preceding sentence): the canonical clause T20 compares against lives in kind_definitions.record -- the taxonomy authority at the top of this registry -- and NOT in this row. The earlier text said 'machine-checked against this row's canonical clause', which named the wrong field: T20's phrase is extracted from exactly three places, .kind_definitions.record here, .properties.artifact_manifest.additionalProperties.properties.kind.description in public/api/identity.schema.v1.json, and the pin_policy_rule --arg line in scripts/operator-local/gen-identity.sh. record_caveat is not one of the three, and a scan of this registry finds the clause in kind_definitions.record only. This row's record_caveat is UNCHECKED prose about how far the api/archive/ naming scheme reaches, and describing it as machine-checked claimed a guarantee nothing provides. Do not restore the earlier claim. docs/IDENTITY_VERIFICATION.md explains the same facts in its own operator-facing prose, deliberately not verbatim -- it says plainly that pin_policy explains itself without reference to that document -- so it must not contradict this row, but is not held to matching it word for word. CORRECTED 2026-08-17: an earlier draft of this sentence claimed docs/IDENTITY_VERIFICATION.md also carries the same wording and must stay in step; that overstated what T20 actually enforces (T20 does not check that file) and understated the gap between a declared obligation and a checked one. Do not restore the earlier claim. anchor-receipt-<tx_id>.json is weaker again: it is named by the transaction id (scripts/gen-anchor-receipt.sh:405), which binds nothing at all about its contents, and it carries generated_at (:314) under the same unconditional rename (:412), so re-running the generator for one tx writes different bytes to the same URL. In practice each receipt is produced once, immediately after its broadcast, so that URL is stable by operating discipline only. Whoever acts on kind=record for this prefix (C4) pins the anchor-source half only, re-derives the three roots from the fetched bytes rather than trusting the file's own dag_root_computed field, and treats a regeneration of either half as a re-pin event. The superseded text justified STRUCTURALLY immutable with a grep of gen-anchor-source.sh for generated_at returning zero hits: the grep was accurate, the field is spelled computed_at, and the conclusion did not follow. Do not restore it.
publications.note: kind=record for the prefix. This is the shape the spec's kind discipline wants api/anchor-source.json to move to (C4). Read record_caveat before pinning anything here: the naming scheme reaches less far than kind=record on its own suggests, and it reaches nothing at all on the receipt half.

owner.producer_evidence: scripts/peer-validators.sh:252 SNAPSHOT_DIR="${STATE_DIR}/peers-history" (master), :284 PUBLISH_DIR="${ROOT}/public/api/peers-history" (repo-local staging), pushed at :336 fyd_push "peers-history/peers-${date}.json.gz"

publications.note: kind=stream, NOT record, and the date key does not make it one. Measured 2026-08-07: scripts/peer-validators.sh:254-256 recomputes SNAPSHOT="${SNAPSHOT_DIR}/peers-${TODAY}.json.gz" and gzips peers.json over it on EVERY run, and :361 calls publish_snapshot_date "$TODAY" unconditionally — the PUBLISHED_LEDGER is consulted only to decide whether to APPEND a ledger line (:347) and to drive the past-day backlog loop (:372), never to decide whether to push today. So the published URL for the current UTC day resolves to different bytes several times a day, which is exactly what kind=record forbids. becomes_record_after=utc-day-close is the true, narrower fact: a member stops changing once its UTC day has passed. That qualifier is the only thing that may license pinning a closed day; .kind alone must never be read as permission (see kind_definitions._kind_is_the_floor). The master copy lives in the host state dir, not in the repo — the repo path is a staging mirror.

The directory is one --delete exclude, but the push allowlist names its members individually (schedule.ics and a 16-64 hex token name), so the two push_allowlist_only entries below carry those. Member filenames embed a private token; never committed.

publications.kind_note: kind=static under the definition above (its published bytes change only when a commit changes them). Semantically it is a record — the signed pre-image of one anchor event — served at a mutable URL. The spec calls that the category error behind the 2026-07-07 stale-publication incident and assigns the fix to C4. It is NOT counted as a kind violation here because it is not pinned by anything, so no gate has anything to act on.

push_allowlist_only._comment: Names the push wrapper accepts that are not one-file publications: they are members of the calendar/ directory entry above. Kept out of publications[] so that 'one path, one row' stays true there.

known_kind_violations._comment: Acknowledgement list for the kind gate (kind=stream MUST NOT appear in any pinned_by), following the same expiry design as deploy/identity-pin-baseline.json: an entry suppresses the gate only while the violation it describes is still exactly the violation present. If the named pin disappears from public/api/identity.json's artifact_manifest, or the named path stops being kind=stream, the entry no longer applies and the test reports it as OBSOLETE — so this cannot become a permanent mute. Every entry is a C4 work item. NOT AN ALERT PATH: this gate acts on the registry's own declarations, not on live bytes. It says nothing about whether a pin currently matches; that is scripts/check-identity-pins.sh's job.

measured_against.method: jq over .artifact_manifest of public/api/identity.json; each entry contributes <key>.sha256 and, where present, <key>.schema_sha256

evidence_json.sha256.reason: Push-owned stream regenerated by scripts/gen-evidence.sh on the metal-evidence cron.

validator_json.sha256.reason: Push-owned stream rewritten by scripts/node-info.sh from live metalgo RPC.

cycle_history_jsonl.sha256.reason: Push-owned stream regenerated by scripts/gen-cycle-history.sh on the metal-cycle-history cron. Same structural class as the three above.
cycle_history_jsonl.sha256.note: This is the fourth stream pin and the only one deploy/identity-pin-baseline.json does not list. That is a documentation gap, NOT a gate gap: scripts/check-identity-pins.sh classifies it as stream from deploy/feed-excludes.txt and stream-class pins never alert there, so nothing was being suppressed. Recording it here makes all four visible in one place.

known_doc_drift._comment: Documentation that this registry measured to be WRONG about a fact the registry itself now carries. Same expiry design as everything else here: each entry records the exact wrong text, and the test fails as OBSOLETE the moment the doc is corrected, so the registry cannot go on describing a defect that no longer exists. This block exists because the alternative — leaving the correction only in prose inside owner.producer_evidence — would turn silently false the day someone fixes the doc, which is the same failure mode the drift baselines were built to avoid. Empty 2026-08-14: the one entry this block ever carried (deploy_ownership_matrix.wrong_producer) was resolved by correcting the four matrix rows in docs/DEPLOY_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX.md; T17 requires this block to be empty exactly when that is true.

known_render_drift._comment: Places where a target file's CURRENT bytes are not what this registry would render, recorded rather than fixed because Phase 0 must not modify the target files. Same expiry design as known_kind_violations: each entry pins both what is expected and what is there, so any change to either side makes the entry stop applying and the test reports it as OBSOLETE. Empty 2026-08-14: the one entry this block ever carried (push_allowlist_doc.missing_rows — scripts/push-to-web-host.sh's header table was missing the anchor-receipt.json / anchor-history.jsonl rows) was resolved by adding the two rows, so canonical and as-built render identically again; T5 requires this block to be empty exactly when that is true.

derived._comment: Rendering instructions. Each output declares its own ORDER because the three target files list the same paths in three different orders, and the comment text that belongs to each entry differs per file. tests/publication-registry/ checks that every order list agrees with publications[] in both directions, so an entry cannot be added to one without the other.
